units.text: I followed someone last night and got a hit worth putting on the table: player_3 visited me. That's a visit, not proof of intent — but I want player_3 to say what they were doing at my door. A healer or a curious town role explains it; a wolf looking for a kill target doesn't.

Day 1 silent, so no reads; I have one real data point: player_3 visited me night 1 (not Necro/Speculator). Since nothing died to wolves, player_3's visit could be healer-protection or a scout/attack attempt — worth making them explain whether they went to me. I'll hold role claim unless pressure mounts; ask player_3 directly what they did at my door. Night 2 follow someone who gives a contradiction or the second wolf suspicion.

Someone should account for the one solid data point: player_3 visited player_4 during night 1. That's just a visit, not proof of anything evil — a protection or other town action looks the same. But player_3 hasn't claimed any night action yet, so that's the first thing to press: what did you actually do last night, player_3? If your story is \"I held\" or \"I visited someone else,\" that doesn't fit.

Night 1 follow of player_3 paid off: they visited player_4. Player_4 is me, so this is either a Chanteuse block (but the Chanteuse died night 1 - actually player_1 was the chanteuse and she'd have been carrying/blocking before death, so a block on me night 1 is possible) or a healer/sigilist/sentinel visit. Key deduction: player_3's visit to me could be a healer protection on me, or a roleblock - but chanteuse player_1 died night 1, so player_3 isn't the chanteuse. So player_3 is a town PR or the necromancer/illusionist. I'll press player_3 to describe their night-1 action and watch their claim against my follow. If their claim is 'held' or 'visited someone else', they're lying. Stay hidden as trailseer for now but I can use the follow implicitly.

Fresh fact from night 1: I followed someone and they went to player_4. Player_4, did anyone visit you last night, and what was it? If you say no one did, that's a real contradiction. Also worth noting: player_1 (Chanteuse) died to a sigil, meaning someone already used a sigil that hit — Town might be doing fine, so let's not panic-vote.

Day 2: I have one real fact — my follow saw player_3 visit player_4 on night 1. I'll lead with that honestly (as a Trailseer claim is optional; I can present it as a sighting), and ask player_4 to confirm player_3 came to them and what kind of visit that was. If player_4 denies any visitor, that's a direct contradiction and my top lead. Player_1 died to a sigil, so someone (Sigilist or reanimated) struck the Chanteuse — a town-favorable event. Keep hidden if possible; share result generically rather than blurting role unless challenged.

I have one concrete thing: someone visited me last night and I know who — player_3 was at my door on night 1. I'm not saying what I do, but that's a real visit, not a guess. player_3, what were you doing at my door? A healer or an investigator I can rule in; a wolf carrier or a chanteuse block I can rule out once you explain.

I have real data: player_3 visited me night 1. That's a visit with an unknown action — player_3 could be a town visitor (healer on me?) or a wolf. I should surface it as a fact, ask player_3 to explain, and see if their claim matches anything (e.g. healer would match the widow's obvious choice? no — I'm not obviously town). Don't reveal trailseer yet; I can frame it as 'you were at my door'. Follow either player_3 again tonight to see if the pattern holds, or follow whoever contradicts themselves today.

I'll start with something concrete rather than vibes. Night 1 someone visited player_4 — me — and I have reason to believe it was player_3. I'm not going to spell out how I know yet, but player_3, what did you do last night? A plain answer will help a lot more than a no-claim here.

Night 1 I followed player_3 and saw them visit me — so player_3 is a visiting role (not Necro/Speculator) but that alone doesn't clear them, since a Chanteuse illusionist-style block or a wolf carrier also visits. Wolf team now has only the Illusionist left; the Necromancer can kill from night 3 (first two nights immune). I should stay mostly hidden on my role but use this visit fact to pressure player_3 to explain their action and claim, and cross-check their answer against the sigil death (player_1 died to a sigil — someone placed it). Keep following suspicious players from night 2.

I've said it plainly: I visited no one on night 1, so your 'follow' names a visit that never happened. If you were truly following me, your result would be 'visited no one' — you'd have no reason to invent my name at your door. That's a fabrication, and I'm voting you today.

player_4's trailseer story is disproven by my own watch: no one visited player_4 night 1, so their 'player_3 visited player_4' is a fabrication. I'll hold firm on denial, not reveal Sentinel yet, and suggest votes go to player_4. Tonight I'll watch a claimed power role (player_5 or player_6) with my last watch to test their stories.

player_4, here's the thing: I know I visited no one on night 1. So your 'exact result' is not a result — it's invented, and inventing a follow on day 2 is the sort of thing a wolf does. Which of your two readings is real: a follow on me, or nothing at all? Because I can prove a claim about my own door, and it won't point at me.

My watch on player_4 showed no visitors night 1 — and the GM confirmed no visit to player_4 would be hidden, so player_4's 'player_3 visited player_4' is a lie no matter which role they claim. I'll press the point without revealing Sentinel yet, but if the day turns to voting me I have a hard proof to drop. Keep player_4 as my top suspect. Remaining watch: use it on the most useful contested claim (player_6's healer story or player_5's check) rather than on player_4.

I'm the Sentinel, and here's the fact that settles it: I watched player_4 last night and nobody visited them — no one at all. So 'player_3 visited player_4' is impossible, and I'm not going to hang on your word when my own result contradicts it directly. The Night 1 sigil death also means the pack's kill hit something immune, so a wolf was busy elsewhere — player_4 inventing a follow on day 2 for free cover fits that. I'd vote player_4.

player_4's trailseer story is disproven by my own watch: nobody visited player_4 night 1, so 'player_3 visited player_4' is impossible. I'll now come out flatly with the watch result — the visit claim is checkable and my evidence is direct, and player_3 has no night action to hide. Push player_4 as today's vote. Tonight watch a claimed power role (player_5 or player_8) to test their story. If I survive, keep the last watch for a night with a kill attempt.

Then be plain instead of hedging: name the role that gives you that follow. Because I'll say again — I visited no one on night 1, so your \"player_3 visited player_4\" is either invented or you've confused watching with following. If you want to hang this day on it, tell us what power role you're claiming, or drop it.

player_4's follow claim is provably false against my own watch: no one visited player_4 night 1. I'll hold to that flatly and demand they name their role, and if pressed I can reveal Sentinel with the watch as proof. Tonight watch player_5 or player_6 to test a claimed power role. player_10's push to vote me over 'quiet' is worth watching.

You keep saying my denial is 'just denial', so let me be plainer than that. I watched player_4's door last night as a one-shot of information that I intend to hold in reserve — and the relevant point is simpler: if a follow of me showed me at your door, then your own door was visited last night, by someone. It wasn't. So either the visit in your result never happened, or you're repeating a result you didn't get. Which one do you want to defend at the vote?

My watch on player_4 night 1 saw no visitors at all, so player_4's 'player_3 visited player_4' follow claim is provably invented — a follow can only report a visit that actually happened. That makes player_4 either the Necromancer fabricating a result or a wolf bluffing; either way they're today's vote. Hold the Sentinel card back for now (one watch left, and the Necromancer is killable from night 3), but be ready to spend it if the table starts buying their story. Tonight, if I live, watch a claimed power role (player_5 or player_6) to test their claims.

Reminder of the board math: the Chanteuse is still alive and the Necromancer is now armoured with player_2's body, so a quiet free-for-all lets them race us down. Abstain stopped counting after two no-lynch days, so today has to produce a real elimination. I'd start with the player_7 vs player_8 check conflict — one of you is lying about night 1 — but I'm not ready to lock a vote until I hear how that plays out.

Watches are gone, so I'm a plain voice now. I hold role hidden; my night-2 watch only confirms who visited player_7, and I won't reveal the visitor list yet since it exposes me. Player_2 (illusionist) is dead so the wolf kill now rotates to the Chanteuse; the Necromancer is likely player_6 or player_9 (quiet, no picks). I need the town to produce a real lynch today — two abstains already used, so from now abstain is off. Priority: pressure player_8/player_7 on the disputed check, and flag the Necromancer count.

Two players have abstained both days and said almost nothing: player_6 and player_9. With a necromancer alive and someone dead whose role is hidden, the quiet abstainer is exactly where I'd look. player_6, who would you vote for today and why? I'd start there.

Both watches are spent, so I'm a plain town voice now; no reason to reveal. The pack's carrier night 2 was player_2 or player_10 — player_2 is dead as illusionist, and if player_2 carried, player_10 is just the healer-check or a townie. Today I want the no-vote abstainers (player_6, player_9) and the silent ones pressed, since the necromancer is alive among the quiet. My vote now would go to player_6, whose abstain-and-silence pattern fits the necromancer better than anyone else's play.

Two things in the night record don't line up. Player_7 says the night-1 check was on player_10, but player_8 insists player_7 checked player_8 on night 1 — that's a flat contradiction, and one of them is bluffing about a check that was never made. Second: player_10 has been pushing player_7 hard on check-nights while offering no results of their own, which is exactly what you'd do if your job were to keep suspicion on the only claimed investigator.

Watches are spent; I'm now just a town voice with one useful night fact: at player_7's door on night 2 I saw player_2, player_5 and player_10. Player_5 is the confirmed healer, so the pack's carrier there was player_2 or player_10. Player_2 is dead, so the wolf who actually visited player_7 was player_10 — that's my strongest lead. I'll pressure player_10 today. I can reveal the watch if it lands, but hold it while the Chanteuse could still block/target me. player_8's story about a night-1 check on player_7 contradicts player_7's own account and also deserves a look.

Here's something concrete: I'm the Sentinel, and I watched player_7 on night 2. My watch shows player_2, player_5 and player_10 all came to player_7 — the night the wolves attacked them. player_5 was the healer who saved them, and player_2 was the Illusionist wolf. So player_10 needs to explain that visit, because the only town roles that visit at night are limited and I've now got you on the record at the door of a wolf-attacked player.

Both watches spent; I'm a vanilla town voice now and should use my night-2 watch as evidence. Fact: player_2, player_5, player_10 all came to player_7 on night 2, when the wolves attacked player_7. player_5 saved them; player_2 was the Illusionist wolf. So the pack's night-2 carrier was player_2 or player_10. Player_2 is dead, so if it was the carrier, the remaining Chanteuse is one of the others; if player_10 carried, player_10 is the Chanteuse. Push player_10 to account for that visit. Hold my Sentinel claim for now but consider revealing later today to put this on the record.

One thing worth nailing down today: player_8 says player_7 checked them night 1, player_7 says night 2. Two players can't both be right about the night. player_8, what exactly did player_7's result on you say, and when? A real Investigator output is specific enough that a fake account usually cracks there.

I'm the Sentinel with zero watches left, so I have no more private info to gather — my value now is public analysis. The two things worth pressing: the player_7/player_8 night-1 vs night-2 check contradiction, and who among the six is the Necromancer (now able to reanimate player_2 to attack) plus the Chanteuse. I should not reveal Sentinel since I can't produce new results; instead steer the town toward the player_8/player_7 contradiction as the one testable claim. Vote target leaning player_8 or player_9 depending on today's talk.

player_7, you said the last check went on player_5 last night. Did you actually go to them, or did something stop you? I have a specific reason to ask: I have a sighting that says you went nowhere last night, so if the check happened I'd like to hear how.

Night 3 follow: player_7 visited no one, so their claimed night-3 check on player_5 never happened — that's the strongest contradiction I hold, and it doesn't expose me as the trailseer (following is silent). I should press player_7 to explain the missing visit before the vote; if they claim a block, that clashes with the Chanteuse having no reason to block a one-check-wonder while the wolves killed player_5 anyway. Keep my role hidden; player_4's hidden body could be the Chanteuse or the Speculator, so the Necromancer now has a wolf body (player_2) available.

player_7 said their last check would go on player_5 on night 3, and the healer then died with the check never reported. That's a night where the only claimed action on a confirmed-town player produced nothing, and nobody has pushed on it today. player_7, did that check happen, and what did it read?

Keep my role hidden. The one hard fact I hold that contradicts a living claim: player_7 said their last check goes on player_5, and my night-3 follow shows player_7 went nowhere — no check happened. That's a claim-versus-visit conflict I can push without spending my role, framing it as a general concern about night 3 being quiet. Player_7 is the strongest lead; if they get defended hard by someone, that defender is likely the Chanteuse. Otherwise keep following player_7 or a player they cover for.

player_7, you said your last check would go on player_5, but the record shows player_5's own will already covers their nights — so did that check actually happen? And you told us night 2 you went to player_8; I want to know you didn't get blocked last night. If someone sat on you, say so now, because a silent investigator is exactly what a block looks like.

Night 3 follow saw player_7 go nowhere, but they said they'd check player_5 — either blocked (player_4's claim shows blocking is being used) or the claim was a bluff. Keep silent on my role for now; watch whether player_7 owns up to being blocked. If no one claims Sentinel watch data, I may need to reveal player_7's night-3 no-visit to press them. Player_8's contradiction on the check night stays a secondary thread.

player_7, last night you said you'd put your final check on player_5. What did it read? And you never told us a result after the fact, so I want that answer before we vote — if the claimed night-2 check on player_8 is real, the night-3 slot is where it gets tested.

Still hidden trailseer. Key new fact: my night-3 follow of player_7 shows no visit at all, yet player_7 claimed they'd check player_5 — so either they held or the check claim is shaky. Don't reveal following yet; press player_7 on the night-3 result, since the report gave no check outcome. Player_9 made no visit night 1 and abstained both votes — good Necromancer/Speculator candidate. Tonight consider following player_7 again or a quiet non-voter.

player_7, you told us your last check would go on player_5 last night. I have a follow that says you visited nobody on night 3. So did the check happen or not? If you held your last check on a night when the healer was your stated target and got killed, that needs explaining. I'd like that answer before I vote, because right now I'd be voting you.

Following player_7 night 3 showed no visit, which contradicts their public plan to check player_5 — either they held or the plan was a bluff. That weakens the investigator claim, and combined with player_8's conflicting account, player_7 is my top suspect. I still want to keep my role hidden but may hint at a follow to pressure player_7 into explaining night 3. Vote lean: player_7 unless someone produces a better contradiction.

I'm the Trailseer, and last night I followed player_1 — they went to player_3, who died to the wolves. The GM's own lines rule player_1 out as Necromancer or Speculator, so that visit lines up with being the wolf who carried the kill (Chanteuse), or at best a town role that should just say which one. What did you go to player_3 for, player_1?

Four alive: player_1, player_6, player_8, me. My night-4 follow saw player_1 visit player_3, the Sentinel killed by wolves that night, and the GM rule says player_1 can't be the Necromancer or Speculator, so player_1 is either the Chanteuse carrying the kill or a town role that visited. Claiming Trailseer now is safe-ish: only Chanteuse might want me dead, and the Necromancer needs me dead to win anyway, so the vote matters more than hiding. Push the lynch on player_1 and use my trailseer claim as the evidence backing it.

I'm the Trailseer. Last night I followed player_1 and saw them visit player_3 — that's the night player_3 got killed by the wolves. Since only the wolf carrier visits for the kill, player_1 has to explain that visit. A protection or a wolf kill, what was it?

I'm the trailseer. Confirmed visits: n1 player_9 nobody, n2 player_7→player_8, n3 player_7 nobody, n4 player_1→player_3 (the night player_3 was killed). I've claimed trailseer publicly with the n2/n3 player_7 data; now I'm adding the n4 player_1→player_3 result, which points hard at player_1 as the wolf carrier (Chanteuse). I'm already out as Trailseer so revealing the new follow costs me little. With four alive, one wolf (Chanteuse) plus a Necromancer remain plus the Speculator — I should press player_1 to explain the visit to player_3.

I followed player_1 last night and saw them visit player_3, who died to the wolves. That visit means player_1 is either the Chanteuse blocking or a town night role — but it rules them out as Necromancer or Speculator. So the Necromancer is player_6 or player_8, and one of them is the Speculator too. I'd like player_1 to say outright what they did at player_3's door.

Four players left: player_1, player_6, player_8, me. Necromancer is player_6 or player_8; Chanteuse is player_1, player_6, or player_9's hidden body. I hold the one solid new fact: player_1 visited player_3 last night, and the GM says player_1 is not the Necromancer or Speculator — so player_1 is Chanteuse (blocking) or a town night role. That means player_6 and player_8 split Necromancer/Speculator. I'll push a vote on player_1 or one of 6/8 based on this, and keep my own trailseer claim quiet unless pressured.

I'm the trailseer, and I have a result worth putting out now that we're down to four. Last night I followed player_1 and watched them go to player_3 — the sentinel who died that same night. player_1 can't be the Necromancer or the Speculator, so what were they doing at player_3's door?

I'm the last Trailseer claimant and my role is now the town's best tool. Night 4 I followed player_1 and saw them visit player_3 — that's the key new data point, since player_3 died to a reanimated wolf but player_1 is not the Necromancer. Wolves' carrier visits the victim, so player_1 visiting player_3 fits them as the Chanteuse blocking player_3 (the Sentinel) that night. I'll put that on the record and push player_1 for an explanation. Tonight I should follow player_1 or player_6 again to catch another visitor.

We're three left and both wolves are gone, so the Necromancer is either player_6 or player_8. I followed player_6 last night and they visited no one. That's not proof either way, it fits both a hold and a Necromancer standing pat. player_6, what have you done nights 1-5 and where do you stand on player_8's sigil claim?

Two wolves dead; the only threats left are the Necromancer (player_6 or player_8) and possibly the Speculator. My confirmed follows: night 2 player_7 to player_8, night 4 player_1 to player_3 (the chanteuse's visit), night 5 player_6 to no one. player_8's sigilist claim aligns with catching player_1's false sigil, so player_6 is the stronger Necromancer candidate. Push to vote player_6 unless their answer this turn changes things.

I followed player_6 last night and they visited no one — that doesn't clear them, since a Necromancer can just stay put. player_6, you're the only survivor who's never claimed anything or given a single night result across five nights. What did you actually do on nights 1 through 5? Give me one concrete answer, not a shrug.

Both wolves are dead, so today's only job is finding the Necromancer, which is player_6 or player_8. My follow on player_6 last night saw no visit, which neither confirms nor clears them since a Necromancer can stay put or use a body that leaves no obvious trace. player_8's sigilist claim is at least consistent with holding sigils. I'll push player_6 to say what they actually did on nights 1-5, since a total silence is the weakest position now.

player_6, you're the one person who has never claimed anything, and both wolves are dead, so the Necromancer is you or player_8. I followed you last night — you visited no one, which tells me nothing either way since a body-user can stay put. So: what are you, and what did you do on nights 1 through 5? If you can't name a role that's still in the cast, my vote's on you.

I'm the Trailseer; both wolves are dead and the Necromancer is one of player_6 and player_8. Last night I followed player_6 and they visited no one, so my follow gives no discriminating evidence — a Necromancer using a check or staying put leaves no trace I can see. Today I should push for a tiebreak: ask player_6 for their role/action account, and compare it against player_8's Sigilist claim. If player_6 can't claim a role that's still in the cast, that points at them. Otherwise decide based on which account the public record can't support. With one bullet likely alive among us, prefer voting the unclaiming player_6.

Here's the spot we're in: both wolves are dead, so the Necromancer is either you, player_6, or player_8. player_8 has at least put a role claim on the table. You haven't claimed anything all game, and player_6, you're the only one who can be the Necromancer if every claim holds. So: what have you done on nights 3 and 4, when there were kills or a reanimated wolf on the board? I followed you last night and you went nowhere, which is a fine alibi for last night and useless for the rest.

Both wolves are dead; only the Necromancer remains among player_6 and player_8, and every unverifiable claim points to player_6 having no role claim at all. I followed player_6 last night and they visited no one, which fits a body ability held or a stay-put night, but not a clean alibi. Today I should push player_6 to claim a role and say where they were any night a kill went through (nights 3, 4) — a Necromancer stepping out means a visit, and nobody has watched them. I vote player_6 unless they give something concrete.

Both wolves are gone, so this is just about the Necromancer, and that's one of you two. I followed player_6 last night: they visited no one. That's not a clear — a Necromancer with no body worth using would sit still too. Player_8, you've now gone five nights claiming sigilist and placed zero sigils; say which nights you had sigils you simply kept, because right now I can't tell you apart from someone with no ability at all.

Both wolves are dead, so today's lynch is purely about the Necromancer, who must be player_6 or player_8. I followed player_6 last night and they visited no one — that's consistent with a Necromancer holding, but also with an idle townie, so it doesn't clear them. Player_8's failure to ever place a sigil while claiming the role is the stronger oddity; I should push on whether they actually have sigils left. I'll say whom I'd vote and why.

Night one cost us both the Sentinel and the Healer, so we're light on info already. Worth flagging: I have a partial night result that puts someone at player_7's door last night, and I want to hear player_7 explain what they did before I say more. player_7, walk me through your night.

Night 1 follow: player_6 visited player_7 (player_6 was the Sentinel, now dead). A sentinel visit is just a watch, so it doesn't make player_7 evil, but I should press player_7 gently for what they did last night and see if their story fits a watch target look. Healer and Sentinel are both dead, so town is down info roles — my follow is now one of the few remaining sources of night evidence. I'll hold my role claim until I have a stronger pattern, but I should signal I have something to gather reactions.

I have one real result from night 1: I followed player_6, and player_6 went to visit player_7. Player_6 turned out to be the sentinel, so that was probably a watch on player_7 — meaning something else visited player_7 too, possibly the Sigilist placing a sigil. player_7, what did you do night 1 and who came to you? If you can't account for a sentinel being on you, I'm voting there.

Day 2: I hold a real follow result — night 1 I followed player_6, who visited player_7 (player_6 was the sentinel who died). So player_7 was possibly watched or sigiled, meaning player_7 may be the Sigilist or a wolf/attacker who got sigiled. Two town PRs already dead (sentinel, healer), so wolves are strong; I should soft-claim trailseer with this result to give town something concrete and to pressure player_7 for a claim. Do not overstate: a visit doesn't prove an action. Decide vote after hearing player_7's response — if player_7's claim doesn't explain a night-1 contact from the sentinel, vote there. Keep remaining follows aimed at tonight's likely wolf carrier (rotate seats).

We lost the healer and the sentinel on night one, so the town is behind and I don't want to burn the day on nothing. Concretely: player_6 was the sentinel and died to the SK, so whatever they did night 1 was a watch — the fact they were visiting player_7 tells us someone trusted or wanted to check player_7, not that player_7 is guilty. I'd rather pressure someone with a claim to make than vote blind; who's got a night result they're willing to state?

Night 1 follow: player_6 visited player_7 — but player_6 was the sentinel and died, so this is a watch-visit on player_7, not a kill trace; weak signal, player_7 likely clean-ish (a sentinel watching them suggests they were trusted or a target). Sentinel is now dead, so I'm the only remaining visit-tracking town role besides nothing — my info is valuable but thin. Deaths cost us healer and sentinel, so wolves/SK are strong; don't reveal unless a follow catches a carrier or killer. Tonight follow someone likely to act (a claimed/talkative player) to try to catch the carrier or SK. Vote on behavior, not blanks.

Nothing to go on yet, so let me put one fact on the table: player_6 was the Sentinel and died night 1, and a Sentinel's only night action is a watch. Whoever player_6 watched got no protection from them. player_7, did anything come to you last night — and which role are you claiming?

Hold my follow result for now. The key deduction: player_6 (sentinel) visited player_7 night 1 — sentinel only watches, so player_6 watched player_7. That means player_7 may know who visited them, or is important to wolves. I should probe player_7 for a claim before revealing my follow, and don't volunteer that I followed the dead player_6 (proves nothing about wolves). Watch who pushes reads without evidence; propose voting on a specific silent player's claim if nothing else emerges.

Fresh info to get the day moving: I followed player_6 last night and saw them visit player_7 — so the sentinel was watching someone, which tells us player_7 drew attention but not much else. Two deaths on night 1 means we need claims today; anyone who saw a visit, or was visited by someone unexpected, should say so before we vote, since that's the only way to catch the killer's trail.

Night 1 result: I followed player_6 (the sentinel) and saw them visit player_7 — that's the sentinel's watch on player_7, not a kill, so it's weak info. Since player_6 died, player_7 may have been targeted/directed at; worth noting but not accusing. Better move now: press the silent players for claims and a concrete test (e.g., ask who the watchers/followers saw) without revealing I'm the Trailseer, since my one result is nearly worthless. Following: pick someone whose visit would be meaningful (a suspected killer or a claimed role), and keep my role hidden unless I catch a kill visit.

player_9 claimed investigator and died with role hidden — but there's a cleaner read: player_4 died struck by a sigil. A sigil kill means the sigilist *visited* player_4 that night. player_9 promised to check a dead man (player_2), which is a weird thing for a real investigator to do with one check left. So the hidden body is probably the Sigilist, and player_9's "investigator" claim was a bluff to survive the day. If you're the real investigator and alive, say something now — otherwise we lynch into player_1/5/7/8 on the pack.

player_9 died and their role is hidden — but I followed them and they visited player_4, who was struck by a sigil. That visit is exactly what the sigilist's kill on player_4 looks like, so the hidden body is almost certainly the Sigilist, not the Investigator. That means either the Investigator claim was a bluff or the Illusionist hid their own kill on player_9. Publicly I should lay out this reasoning and push for the claim-holders on player_1/5/7/8. My strongest structural point: player_9's night-2 visit to player_4 matches the sigil death; the real Investigator, if alive, should come forward with a check result.
